memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Asher's food will be rich; he will provide delicacies fit for a king. Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.'" — Gen 49:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two brief, gentle blessings. Asher's land will be fertile enough to supply a royal table. Naphtali is pictured as a doe running free, bearing beautiful young.

There is no drama here — no sceptre, no lion, no warning. Just fruitfulness and freedom.

It is worth noticing that God's blessings are not all the same shape. Judah gets the sceptre. Asher gets good farmland. Naphtali gets freedom and beautiful children. Zebulun gets a coastline. None of these is a lesser gift; they are simply different.

We compare our lives against the most visible callings and quietly conclude that we have been given something small. But a life of quiet fruitfulness, feeding others and raising a family well, is a genuine blessing from God — not a consolation prize for those who did not get the sceptre.

Paul makes exactly this point about the church. There are different gifts, different kinds of service, but the same God at work in all of them (1 Cor 12:4-6). The body needs the hand as much as the eye.

Receive the shape of blessing God has actually given you, rather than grieving the shape He gave someone else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What shape has God's blessing taken in your life?
2. Do you value it, or wish it looked like someone else's?
3. Who are you feeding, in some sense, with what God has given you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the particular gifts You have given me. Stop me from grieving what You gave someone else, and help me use what is actually in my hands. Amen.
